criteria.note: JiraCloudAdapter._create_or_update_epic and _create_or_update_child (.warp/tracker_intake.py) are completed against Jira Cloud REST via stdlib urllib (both previously raised 'later increment WARP-1006'). The epic is keyed by the plan id (_warp_marker('epic', key)) and each child by its work item id (_warp_marker('child', epic_key, key)); _upsert_issue creates once via POST /rest/api/3/issue (project + issuetype + summary + the marker label) and updates in place thereafter via PUT /rest/api/3/issue/{key} touching only the summary. Each child is linked to its epic via the Jira parent field ({'parent': {'key': <epic key>}}), the epic resolved (or shell-created) by the SAME epic marker so the child is self-sufficient and both converge on one epic. Auth is the token_ref resolved at __init__ by _default_secret_resolver; the adapter FAILS CLOSED (TrackerAdapterError 'no token resolved') before any write, so no epic/child write is reachable without a credential and no raw credential appears in a file/prompt/proof/log. _set_status is reused for the epic/child status; a create with no project wired fails loud by name. Confirmed by reading the source and driving the adapter's own methods over an injected in-process transport in selftest.

UPSERT NEVER FORKS holds, honoring the FakeTracker contract (create_or_update_epic/child are upserts keyed by a stable caller identity, find-then-update-else-create). _find_by_marker runs a labels JQL 'labels = "<marker>" ORDER BY created ASC' with maxResults=1 and returns the SAME (oldest) issue on a re-run, so _upsert_issue updates it in place and NEVER creates a second one: a re-run forks no second epic and no duplicate child. The marker is a pure idempotency key (matched exactly, never parsed back, never rewritten on update). _warp_marker is stable and collision-free (same key -> same marker, distinct keys -> distinct markers, child marker carries both epic and work item, label-safe with no whitespace). Fail loud on the unresolvable: a create with no project wired raises TrackerAdapterError by name, a create returning no key raises by name, and the base seam still raises TrackerItemNotFound for a set_status/comment/assign on an object the tracker does not hold. Proven by the selftest teeth (upsert re-run same key adds no create and updates in place; a different work item and a different plan each create a distinct issue; no-project create raises) and by an independent mutation (see findings/teeth).

findings.text: Non-blocking, reference-path only, idempotency-preserving. On the LIVE adapter the epic's secondary routing label (warp-repo-<repo>, added by _issue_labels only on CREATE) is not backfilled on UPDATE, because _upsert_issue deliberately touches only the summary on the update path so the load-bearing marker survives. In the plan-mirror flow (mirror_plan_events) the epic is created first WITH fields, so it carries the routing label. But a child upserted through the spec mirror (mirror_events) shell-creates its epic by marker with fields=None, so that epic gets only the marker label and never gains warp-repo-<repo> even after the plan mirror later updates its title. This does not affect the AC2 crux (the marker is always present, so the epic converges to one object and never forks) nor routing correctness (routing is enforced upstream on the plan's tracker_repo and the child link is the parent field, not the label); it only leaves the secondary identifiability label off a shell-first epic. Worth noting for an operator wiring the live mirror.
